_doc: Xianxia v1 dress sheets for every sect (user 2026-11-26). Keys x:<sect>. Each keeps the sect's own marks and says how elders and the head dress richer, so a sect reads as one house and the strong look it.
x:bang_tam: Băng Tâm Các, the Ice sect of the frozen north: flowing layered robes of white silk and frost-pale gauze, three crossed collars edged in ice blue, wide sleeves embroidered at the cuffs with silver snowflakes and frost ferns, a sash of shimmering frost silk hung with a white jade pendant; elders wear a pale blue gauze over-robe that drifts like mist; hair long, dressed with white jade or silver hairpins.
x:coc_vu: Cốc Vũ Quán, the rain-calling rice abbey: soft robes of rain-grey and rice-green silk, a pale grey gauze over-robe beaded as if with dew, collars embroidered with falling rain and rice ears, a sash with a small green jade drop; a light rice-straw hat on a silk cord for the terraces.
x:da_quang: Dạ Quang Môn, the night-glow riders of the desert edge: robes of deep night-blue and dune-gold silk, a flowing sand-coloured gauze over-robe, collars embroidered with crescent moons and stars in pale gold, a sash with a glowing jade cup; hair bound under a dark silk headwrap with a gold pin.
x:muc_van: Mục Vân Trang, the cloud-herder horse manor of the western plain: riding robes of fine grass-green and cloud-white silk, a sky-blue gauze over-robe, collars embroidered with running horses and clouds, a broad sash with a white jade horse; hair in a high knot with a silver ring.
x:phat_y: Phất Y Cốc, the valley of hired swords: long robes of fine grey silk with a silver-grey gauze over-robe, the left sleeve long and flowing past the hand, collars edged in charcoal, a narrow sash with a small silver sword-token; hair bound in a high knot with a plain silver crown.
x:phuong_minh: Phượng Minh Cung, the Fire court of the phoenix: splendid layered robes of vermilion, gold and dawn-orange silk, collars and hems embroidered with phoenix feathers and flames in gold thread, wide trailing sleeves, a gold sash with red jade; hair piled high with gold phoenix hairpins and a small flame-shaped crown.
x:thien_xu: Thiên Xu Tông, the Pivot of the central plateau: stately robes of deep bronze and earth-gold silk under a dark iron-grey over-robe, collars embroidered with the seven Dipper stars and mountain ridges in gold, a broad sash with a heavy yellow jade seal; elders wear a black silk outer robe with a high collar; hair under a gold or bronze crown.
x:thinh_vu: Thính Vũ Lâu, the Tower Where One Listens to the Rain, a dark Thunder house: robes of black and storm-violet silk, a long black oiled-silk over-robe that falls like rain, collars and cuffs embroidered with silver lightning and raindrops, a sash hung with a bronze bell; hair bound with dark silver hairpins.
x:thu_phan: Thu Phần Các, the ma đạo grave-keepers among the old graves: mourning robes of undyed white and ash-grey silk, a translucent black gauze over-robe like smoke, collars embroidered with withered lotus and grave-incense curls in dull silver, a sash with a dark resentment-jade seal; hair long and loose, held by a single bone hairpin.
x:tung_dao: Tùng Đào Cung, the palace of the pine sea: flowing robes of soft pine-green and pale bark-cream silk, collars and hems embroidered with pine needles and wind-curls in darker green, a needle-green silk sash for inner disciples with a green jade pine-cone pendant; elders wear grey-green gauze over-robes; hair long, pinned with a jade pine-twig hairpin.
x:bach_vu: Bách Vũ Các, bird keepers of the jungle hills: flowing robes of leaf-green and russet silk, over-robes and capelets sewn from shimmering moulted feathers of blue, brown and russet that overlap like scales, collars embroidered with tiny birds in gold thread, a fine leather-and-silk gauntlet on one wrist; elders wear long trailing feather mantles and a feather crown, the head a mantle of a hundred colours.
x:binh_thuy: Bình Thủy Môn, ferry-masters of a sea strait: flowing robes of salt-white and sea-teal silk, a translucent sea-green gauze over-robe that ripples like water, collars embroidered with waves and small boats in silver, a sash of knotted green silk cord with a pale shell pendant; captains wear a dark-amber silk storm-robe over all, the head a pearl-studded collar.
x:chan_kim: Chân Kim Các, the Pavilion of True Gold, assayers of ore and metal: robes of wine-red, mustard and dark-green silk under a short square-shouldered over-robe of deep blue silk, collars embroidered with golden scales and balances, a sash hung with tiny gold weights and a small brass balance; elders wear gold-threaded brocade and a gold crown shaped like a balance beam.
x:chuc_ha: Chức Hà Các, the Pavilion of the Woven Clouds, silk weavers of the south: layered robes of the finest cream silk that seems to glow, a gauze over-robe woven with clouds, sleeves gathered with silk cords; outer disciples a pale beige sash, inner a grey-green sash, fire-setters a deep red sash and a lacquered shuttle in the hair; elders and the head wear woven-cloud brocade that shifts colour like the evening sky.
x:cung_tinh: Củng Tinh Quán, star-watchers of a high plain: robes of dry-grass gold and night-blue silk, a night-blue gauze over-robe scattered with tiny embroidered stars in silver, a hairpin of dark star-iron through the topknot; elders wear star-chart brocade with constellations in silver thread and a crown of dark star-iron.
x:cuu_cao: Cửu Cao Phái, crane riders of the marsh: flowing robes of grey and white silk, over-robes edged with soft white crane down, collars embroidered with flying cranes in silver, a pale grey-and-white crane feather in the hair; grooms wear reed-green silk with the hems tied up; elders wear long white crane-down mantles and a silver crane crown.
x:ham_nguyet: Hàm Nguyệt Trang, the pearl-and-spirit-fish manor of the moon lake: robes of moon-white and evening-blue silk, a translucent pearl-grey gauze over-robe, collars embroidered with fish and moon ripples in silver, a sash of the blue the lake turns at evening, pearl-shell ornaments; divers wear close-fitting sea-grey silk; the mistress wears whatever she likes, with a pearl in each ear and a pearl crown.
x:ho_lam: Hộ Lâm Đường, forest wardens of the northern woods: long robes of bark-brown and deep forest-green silk with a soft sheen, wooden toggles carved like acorns, collars embroidered with oak leaves, a green silk sash, a hatchet or a coil of tally cord; elders wear a dark green gauze over-robe embroidered with whole trees, the head a crown of carved dark wood.
x:hoa_cai: Hoa Cái Đường, a pill house of the badlands: robes of vermilion silk with stiff standing collars embroidered with pill-furnace flames in gold, darker red sashes, gloves of oiled yellow silk; in the mercury room a bronze mask with round crystal eyes hangs at the neck; elders wear crimson brocade over-robes and a red jade crown.
x:hoa_tinh: Họa Tinh Đường, talisman painters of a mountain hall: robes of matte black silk with narrow sleeves, a faint violet sheen from the hall's fungus dye at the collar, a black silk cord at the left wrist, hair bound up with a slim bamboo brush through the knot, ink-dark fingertips; elders wear black gauze over-robes painted with faint silver talisman lines that hold no writing, and a jet hairpin.
x:hong_dau: Hồng Đậu Trang, a manor of red-bean gardens: graceful robes of red and rose silk, a rose gauze over-robe, collars embroidered with red beans and vines in gold, a single bright red bean on a thin red silk string at the throat; in the garden a wide conical hat over the silk; the mistress wears full crimson brocade and a red-bean crown.
x:hong_lo: Hồng Lô Cốc, the furnace valley on the snowy north coast: robes of rust and brick-red silk lined with soft grey seal fur at the collar and cuffs, an ember-red gauze over-robe, collars embroidered with furnace flames and snowflakes, forearms bare in the furnace hall with burn scars worn openly; elders wear white seal-fur mantles over crimson brocade and a bronze crown.
x:lac_ha: Lạc Hà Các, a sunset sect of the western islands: flowing robes of silk dyed the colours of evening, from pale ochre to rust to dusk violet, a sunset-gold gauze over-robe, collars embroidered with flying geese and sunset clouds in gold; outer disciples ochre, inner rust, true disciples and elders dusk violet; small hall pins (a grey goose feather, a stern-lamp clasp, a pressed red maple leaf); the head wears the founder's robe of all the evening colours.
x:lang_dao: Lãng Đào Môn, ferry families of the Nine-Bend River: robes of river-green and tar-black silk with a glossy sheen, a translucent river-grey gauze over-robe, collars embroidered with waves and river bends in silver, a wide straw hat on a silk cord; inner disciples a green silk headcloth; elders a silver-blue gauze over-robe and a jade boat-pole pin.
x:lanh_giang: Lãnh Giang Phái, the ice-hole sitters of the frozen Hàn Giang: quilted robes of indigo-grey silk with crossed collars and frost-white toggles, a straw-gold rain cape woven fine as silk over the shoulders, a wide straw hat tied with a blue cord, collars embroidered with frozen ripples; elders wear frost-white gauze over-robes and silver hairpins like icicles.
x:le_hoa: Lê Hoa Am, the hermitage of the pear blossom: white nuns, heads shaved smooth, wear flowing robes of white wool-silk with high crossed collars, wide sleeves and white sashes, pale pear-wood beads at the neck, pear blossoms embroidered in white at the hem; grey sisters keep their hair and wear soft grey silk; the abbess adds a sheer white veil-robe that drifts like blossom.
x:le_tuyen: Lễ Tuyền Phái, healers and wine-brewers of the lake meadows: robes of fine spring-green silk with crossed collars and white silk sashes, collars embroidered with healing herbs and wine cups in silver, a roll of silver needles in green silk at the sash; brewers wear amber silk; elders wear pale jade-green gauze over-robes and a jade crown.
x:minh_loan: Minh Loan Các, the Pavilion of the Singing Bells, bronze casters: robes of bronze-brown and gold silk with round collars embroidered with bells and sound-ripples in gold, a small bronze bell at the sash; casters wear clay-grey silk over-robes; elders wear bronze-gold brocade and a crown of tiny bells.
x:nam_pho: Nam Phố Đường, dawn talisman scribes of a river shore: robes of mulberry-grey silk under a pale dawn-pink gauze over-robe, collars embroidered with ink-wash clouds, faint ink at the cuffs; scribes of the dusk line add a violet hem; the hall-mistress pins her hair with a jade-handled writing brush and wears dawn-gold brocade.
x:ngao_tuyet: Ngạo Tuyết Phái, the School That Defies the Snow, mountain swordsmen: flowing white silk robes in every season, a wide white sash, collars embroidered with plum branches in pale pink, a dark plum-wood pin with two or three tiny pink blossoms in the hair; elders wear a white gauze over-robe that drifts like snow and a silver crown with plum blossoms.
x:nhan_tran: Nhạn Trận Môn, a war-formation gate of the lake plain: short-skirted robes of grey-brown silk with standing collars and narrow sleeves, embroidered with geese flying in formation in silver, a braided silk belt, a grey goose feather in the hair (the head's is the longest); elders wear dark grey gauze over-robes and a silver goose crown.
x:nhan_van: Nhàn Vân Quán, the abbey of painters: soft robes of undyed grey silk, the sleeve ends stained solid black with ink, a pale ink-wash gauze over-robe painted with drifting clouds, hair knotted and pinned with a painter's brush; painters of the Pool House wear a thin blue silk thread at the collar; the head's brush is the oldest, and she wears a cloud-painted brocade.
x:phan_vu: Phần Vũ Đường, body cultivators of the vent country: bare-armed robes of dark-red and ember silk with a wide crimson sash embroidered with flames, sleeveless over-robes, a pale scar line from wrist to shoulder for every sitting; elders' arms are white with fine lines and they wear crimson brocade mantles over one shoulder and a red jade crown.
x:suong_tung: Sương Tùng Các, the Pavilion of Frost and Pine, talisman writers of the pine lake: robes of frost-white and pine-green silk, a frost-pale gauze over-robe, collars embroidered with pine needles rimed with frost, ink on the cuffs; outer disciples a pale grey sash, inner a pine-green sash, elders and the head a dark green sash and a jade pine hairpin.
x:tam_kiem: Tầm Kiếm Đường, mountain hunters and cave-searchers: robes of forest-brown and moss-green silk cut for climbing, a short quilted silk jerkin, silk climbing cord over one shoulder, a sword with a notch-filed crossguard (one notch per cave searched); elders wear a dark moss-green gauze over-robe embroidered with mountain caves and a bronze crown.
x:thai_chi: Thải Chi Cốc, herb-pickers of a terraced valley: robes of cream and herb-green silk with the sleeves rolled, a cream silk overskirt for the terraces, collars embroidered with herbs and terrace lines, a silk satchel of herbs; elders wear jade-green gauze over-robes embroidered with every herb of the valley and a jade herb hairpin.
x:thien_bao: Thiên Bảo Trai, the refiners-and-auction house of the western steppe: perfectly pressed robes of pale grey silk so that the goods are the only colour in the room, a refiner's thin red-gold thread round each cuff, an appraiser's at the collar edge; elders wear silver-grey brocade with red-gold edging; the mistress wears one red-gold pin and the finest grey silk.
x:thoi_tinh: Thối Tinh Môn, smiths of an iron mountain: robes of dark iron-grey and ember-red silk with short sleeves showing bare forearms, a black silk forge apron embroidered with sparks in gold, an iron thumb-ring; the head's apron is edged in red-gold; elders wear black brocade with molten-gold embroidery and an iron crown.
x:thuy_vi: Thúy Vi Tông, the green-haze herb and pill sect of the south-west: flowing robes of green-grey silk dyed with haze-grown indigo, a translucent green gauze over-robe like haze, collars embroidered with herbs and mist in silver; outer disciples a plain grey sash, inner a pale green silk collar and a dark green cord, true disciples a jade herb pendant; elders and the head wear jade-green brocade and a jade crown.
x:trac_anh: Trạc Anh Đài, seal and whale hunters of the frost coast: close-fitting robes of sea-grey and black silk lined with soft seal fur, collars closed with pale walrus-ivory toggles, embroidered with waves and whales in silver, silk hat-strings tied under the chin; elders wear white-fur mantles and an ivory crown.
x:tran_sa: Trấn Sa Đường, caravan guards of the desert road: long hooded robes of sand-gold silk over dark-brown silk, collars embroidered with dunes and caravan stars, silk-wrapped vambraces, a sabre on the LEFT hip, a small horn whistle on a cord; elders wear dark-gold gauze over-robes and a gold headpiece.
x:truc_thuc: Trúc Thực Viên, the garden of the bamboo seed: robes of pale straw-gold bamboo silk with a fine woven grain, collars embroidered with bamboo leaves in green, a conical hat of split bamboo on a silk cord; elders wear jade-green gauze over-robes embroidered with bamboo groves and a jade bamboo hairpin.
x:tuan_tung: Tuần Tùng Đường, the hall of the pine wardens: robes of grey silk with wolf-fur trim at the collar, embroidered with running wolves in silver; outer wardens a strip of wolf fur at the collar, inner wardens a wolf-fur half-cape over the left shoulder, elders a full grey wolf mantle and a silver wolf-head clasp; a bone whistle on a cord.
x:van_hac: Vạn Hác Viện, a zither academy of the pine ravines: flowing robes of soft grey silk with wide sleeves and a silk cord sash, collars embroidered with zither strings and ravine pines; players of the sixth movement grow the right-hand nails long, hard and pale; the head wears a pale ravine-blue gauze over-robe and a jade zither pin.
x:van_khoi: Vân Khởi Tự, an abbey of sitters on a bare mountain: plain flowing robes of cloud-grey silk with a rope-silk belt, a neat square of the same silk at each knee from sitting on rock (the abbey's mark of practice), collars embroidered faintly with rising clouds; the head wears nothing more; the Reader alone carries a small bronze hand bell.
x:vong_trieu: Vọng Triều Đường, the Hall Watching the Tide, lamp-keepers of the western towers: knee-length robes of oiled grey silk closed with brass toggles, collars embroidered with tides and lamp-rays in gold, a brass lamp-hook at the sash; elders carry a lit storm lamp and wear a gold-threaded grey brocade.
x:vu_an: Vụ Ẩn Môn, the gate hidden in mist: long hooded robes of grey-green silk that seem to dissolve into mist at the hem, collars embroidered with mist curls in silver, a wide round hat of fine bamboo on a silk cord, a lantern on a cord; elders wear robes of pure mist-grey gauze and a silver lantern pin.
x:vu_linh: Vũ Linh Đường, bell-casters of the forest roads: robes of charcoal-grey silk with narrow sleeves, collars embroidered with warning bells in bronze thread, a small bronze bell (cast at their first pour, unmarked) on a cord at the chest; casters wear scorched silk aprons; elders wear bronze-grey brocade and a crown of small bells.
x:xuyen_lam: Xuyên Lâm Môn, guides and staff fighters of the rain-forest road: robes of forest-brown, olive and grey-green silk with crossed collars and woven silk belts, a straw rain cape fine as silk (gold straw for the young, silver-grey for elders), a bamboo staff; elders wear deep olive gauze over-robes embroidered with jungle vines.
x:yen_quang: Yên Quang Các, alchemist-pickers of the evening glow: robes of smoke-grey silk with sleeves tied back by violet cords, a violet gauze over-robe the colour of evening glow, collars embroidered with herbs and evening clouds, an herb pouch at the hip; inner disciples a sprig of their first herb at the collar; the head and elders a pale violet inner collar and an amethyst hairpin.
